# Node reference

Every built-in node type with its inputs, outputs and params, by family. A param marked with a group, like *(more)*, sits in that folded section of the param          panel. A soft range is only the slider's; typed values outside it are kept. For what the families are for, see [Concepts](../concepts.md).

Families: [tex](#tex), [chan](#chan), [table](#table), [geo](#geo), [mat](#mat), [light](#light), [view](#view), [script](#script), [out](#out), [comp](#comp)

### tex.blobtrack

Finds blobs (people, hands, spots of light) and follows them with ids that stay

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)
- `background` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex), `blobs` (table), `chans` (chan).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detect` | background \| bright | `"background"` |  | background: what differs from the empty scene (the `background` input where connected, else learned: `blobtrack.learn`); bright: whatever is brighter than `threshold` |
| `threshold` | float | `0.1` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Difference to the background (in any channel), or brightness, from which a pixel counts |
| `adapt` | float | `30` | 0 to 300 s (soft) | How soon a lasting change (light, a moved chair) becomes background; someone standing still fades ten times slower. 0: never |
| `min_area` | float | `0.1` | 0 to 5 % (soft) | Smaller blobs are ignored (of the picture's area) |
| `max_area` | float | `50` | 1 to 100 % (soft) | Larger blobs are ignored (the whole room changing is not a blob) |
| `max_blobs` | int | `16` | 1 to 32 (soft) | Most blobs, the largest |
| `show` | overlay \| mask \| difference \| background | `"overlay"` |  | What `out` shows: the picture with the blobs marked, the pixels counted, the difference (the threshold is mid grey) or the learned background |
| `size` *(more)* | int | `320` | 64 to 960 px (soft) | Width the input is analysed at; more finds smaller things and costs more |
| `open` *(more)* | int | `1` | 0 to 6 px (soft) | Removes specks and lines thinner than twice this (at the analysed size) |
| `close` *(more)* | int | `2` | 0 to 6 px (soft) | Fills holes and joins parts closer than twice this |
| `reach` *(more)* | float | `0.15` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | How far a blob may jump between frames and keep its id, beyond where its speed puts it (of the width) |
| `hold` *(more)* | float | `0.5` | 0 to 5 s (soft) | A blob gone for less keeps its id when it comes back |
| `slots` *(more)* | int | `4` | 0 to 8 (soft) | Blobs in `chans`, each as id, x, y, area with the slot's number (id 0: empty) |

### tex.cache

The last frames of the input; outputs one of them, some frames back

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | int | `30` | 1 to 240 f (soft) | Frames kept (at most 2 GiB of them) |
| `index` | int | `0` | 0 to 239 f (soft) | How many frames back the output is; 0 is the newest |
| `record` | bool | `true` |  | Take new frames; off holds what is kept |
| `persist` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | While not recording, keep the held frames in the state snapshots, so they survive a restart |

### tex.chromakey

Make pixels near a key colour transparent (green or blue screen)

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | colour | `[0, 1, 0, 1]` |  | The screen's colour |
| `tolerance` | float | `0.1` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Chroma distance from the key that is fully transparent |
| `softness` | float | `0.08` | 0 to 0.5 (soft) | Width of the soft edge beyond it |
| `spill` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | How much of the key's tint is removed from what stays |
| `invert` | bool | `false` |  | Keep the key colour, drop the rest |
| `output` | keyed \| matte | `"keyed"` |  | The keyed image, or its alpha as white on black |

Inputs:

- `bottom` (tex)
- `top` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | over \| add \| multiply \| screen \| subtract \| difference \| maximum \| minimum \| average \| inside \| outside \| atop \| overlay | `"over"` |  | inside, outside: the top only where the bottom is, or is not; atop: the top over the bottom, only where the bottom is; overlay: darkens the dark and brightens the bright parts of the bottom by the top |
| `swap` | bool | `false` |  | Swap the inputs: bottom onto top (TouchDesigner's Swap Operation Order) |

### tex.denoise

Calms a noisy picture (a camera in the dark): averages over frames where it is still

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | float | `8` | 1 to 64 (soft) | About how many frames are averaged where the picture is still, for brightness noise; more is calmer; 1: off |
| `color_frames` | float | `8` | 1 to 64 (soft) | The same for colour noise (coloured speckles) |
| `motion` | float | `0.06` | 0 to 0.3 (soft) | A change from which a pixel counts as moving and shows the new frame at once (on the square root of the values, so it means about the same in dark and bright parts). Raise it when the noise still flickers, lower it when moving things leave trails |
| `spatial` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | Smooths the brightness of what moves, where the average cannot help, keeping edges stronger than `motion`; 0: off |
| `color_spatial` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 (soft) | The same for the colour; the eye forgives soft colour more than soft brightness |
| `reset` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Forget the average, while on |

### tex.feedback

A loop: wire the end of the chain back into `previous`; `initial` until that has a frame

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs:

- `initial` (tex)
- `previous` (tex) Sees the previous frame, so it may close a loop.

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reset` | bool | `false` |  | Pass `initial` instead, while on |
| `persist` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | Keep the loop's last frame in the state snapshots, so a restart carries on from it |

Maps a part of its input onto a projector: corners, mesh warp, soft edges with other mappers of the same input

| `blend` | bool | `true` |  | Soft edges where other mappers of the same input overlap this one (off for stacked projectors) |
| `pattern` | bool | `false` |  | An alignment grid of the input instead of the picture |
| `corner_tl` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Top left corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes (drag it in the viewer) |
| `corner_tr` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Top right corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes |
| `corner_br` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Bottom right corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes |
| `corner_bl` *(warp)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -0.5 to 0.5 (soft) | Bottom left corner, moved from its fitted place, in picture sizes |
| `warp` *(warp)* | text |  |  | Mesh warp: one line per grid row, `dx,dy` offsets in picture sizes; empty is none (edit it in the viewer) |
| `blend_gamma` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0.2 to 3 (soft) | Exponent on the soft edge; above 1 darkens the overlap, below 1 brightens it |

### tex.opticalflow

How far each part of the picture moved since the previous frame (optical flow)

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (tex).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `colors` | bool | `false` |  | Show the motion as colours instead of passing the numbers on: direction as hue, speed as brightness. For looking at it; nodes that use the motion want this off |
| `confidence` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Blue says how well the motion is pinned down, 0 to 1: high where there is texture, moving or not, low on a plain wall; off, blue is 0 and a still picture black |
| `fill` | int | `4` | 0 to 6 (soft) | Rounds of filling in: the motion found at edges and texture spreads into plain parts of the same thing (skin, a shirt), not across edges; each round reaches twice as far. 0: off |
| `threshold` | float | `0.25` | 0 to 4 px (soft) | Slower motion than this fades out (none below half of it), so camera noise does not shimmer; in pixels at the analysed size per frame |
| `size` *(more)* | int | `320` | 64 to 960 px (soft) | Width the input is analysed at, and the output's; more sees finer motion and costs more |
| `levels` *(more)* | int | `4` | 1 to 6 (soft) | Pyramid levels, each half the size of the one before; each one doubles the fastest motion followed |
| `iterations` *(more)* | int | `3` | 1 to 6 (soft) | Refining steps per level; more is more exact and costs more |
| `window` *(more)* | int | `3` | 1 to 6 px (soft) | Radius of the neighbourhood each pixel's motion is judged from; more is smoother and steadier, less keeps small moving things apart |

| `surface` | auto \| material \| texture \| parts \| uv \| normals | `"auto"` |  | auto: the texture input where connected, else the file's materials; parts: a colour per part id |
| `shift` *(camera)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Lens shift in picture sizes: [0, 0.5] moves the picture up by half its height |
| `camera` *(camera)* | text |  |  | A calibrated camera as JSON (calib.solve's `camera`); replaces position, target, fov, roll and shift |

| `far` *(camera)* | float | `100` | 0.001 to 1000000 | Farthest distance drawn |
| `background` *(more)* | colour | `[0, 0, 0, 0]` |  |  |
| `cull` *(more)* | bool | `false` |  | Leave out faces turned away (counter-clockwise is the front) |
| `antialias` *(more)* | bool | `true` |  | Four samples per pixel |
| `shadow_size` *(more)* | int | `2048` | 256 to 4096 (soft) | Texels across each light's shadow map: sharper shadows, more memory |
| `ao` *(occlusion)* | bool | `false` |  | Ambient occlusion: less ambient and environment light in creases and where objects meet; direct light and unlit surfaces stay as they are |
| `ao_radius` *(occlusion)* | float | `0.5` | 0.01 to 2 m (soft) | How far around a point geometry darkens it |
| `ao_strength` *(occlusion)* | float | `1` | 0 to 3 (soft) | How much of the hidden ambient light is taken away: 1 as estimated, 0.3 at most 30 %, above 1 darker |

| `budget` *(more)* | float | `4` | 0.5 to 20 (soft) | Most GPU memory the kept frames take, in GiB; past it fewer are kept, with a warning |

Inputs:

- `in` (geo)

Outputs: `out` (geo).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translate` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -10 to 10 (soft) |  |
| `rotate` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -180 to 180 ° (soft) | About x, then y, then z |
| `scale` | vec3 | `[1, 1, 1]` | 0 to 4 (soft) |  |
| `uniform` | float | `1` | 0.001 to 1000 (soft) | Times the scale: 0.001 turns millimetres into metres |

## mat

[mat.constant](#matconstant), [mat.occluder](#matoccluder), [mat.pbr](#matpbr), [mat.phong](#matphong), [mat.wireframe](#matwireframe)

### mat.constant

A colour as it is, unlit: what projection content wants

Inputs:

- `texture` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (mat).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear RGBA, straight alpha; replaces the file's colour; times the texture input |

### mat.occluder

Invisible, but hides what is behind it: a real object in front of a projection; casts shadows

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (mat).

### mat.pbr

Physically based (metallic, roughness as in glTF): lit by the render's lights, best with an environment light

Inputs:

- `texture` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (mat).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear RGBA, straight alpha; replaces the file's colour; times the texture input |
| `metallic` | float | `0` | 0 to 1 | 0: plastic, paint, glass; 1: metal, whose colour tints its reflections |
| `roughness` | float | `0.5` | 0 to 1 | 0: a mirror; 1: matte |
| `emit` *(more)* | colour | `[0, 0, 0, 1]` |  | Light the surface gives off by itself; alpha is unused |

### mat.phong

Lit by the render's lights, with a highlight; black without lights

Inputs:

- `texture` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (mat).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear RGBA, straight alpha; replaces the file's colour; times the texture input |
| `specular` | colour | `[0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1]` |  | The highlight's colour; alpha is unused |
| `shininess` | float | `32` | 1 to 512 (soft) | Higher: a smaller, sharper highlight |
| `emit` *(more)* | colour | `[0, 0, 0, 1]` |  | Light the surface gives off by itself; alpha is unused |

### mat.wireframe

Only the edges, as lines of a width in pixels, unlit

Inputs:

- `texture` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (mat).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | The lines' colour: linear RGBA, straight alpha; times the texture input |
| `line_width` | float | `1.5` | 0.5 to 8 px (soft) | The lines' width in pixels of the render |
| `edges` | polygons \| triangles | `"polygons"` |  | polygons: leave out edges inside flat faces (a quad's diagonal); triangles: every edge |

## light

[light.ambient](#lightambient), [light.directional](#lightdirectional), [light.environment](#lightenvironment), [light.merge](#lightmerge), [light.point](#lightpoint), [light.projector](#lightprojector), [light.spot](#lightspot)

### light.ambient

Light from everywhere alike, also where a surface faces away

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (light).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear; alpha is unused |
| `intensity` | float | `0.2` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Times the colour |

### light.directional

Parallel light from far away, as the sun

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (light).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | vec3 | `[-2, -3, 4]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Where it shines from; only the direction to the target counts |
| `target` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | What it shines at |
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear; alpha is unused |
| `intensity` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Times the colour |
| `shadows` | bool | `false` |  | What stands in its way casts a shadow |
| `bias` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Shadow offset, times the usual: more against stripes on lit surfaces, less against light leaking where objects touch |

### light.environment

Light from a picture of everything around (equirectangular): soft light and reflections

Inputs:

- `texture` (tex)

Outputs: `out` (light).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear; alpha is unused |
| `intensity` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Times the colour |
| `turn` | float | `0` | -180 to 180 ° (soft) | About z, counter-clockwise seen from above; at 0 the picture's middle looks along +x, as in Blender |
| `size` *(more)* | int | `1024` | 128 to 2048 (soft) | Texels across the baked reflections: sharper mirrors, more memory and a longer bake |

### light.merge

The lights of several inputs, for one render

Inputs:

- `in0` (light)
- `in1` (light)
- `in2` (light)
- `in3` (light)

Outputs: `out` (light).

### light.point

Light from a point, in every direction

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (light).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | vec3 | `[1.5, -2.5, 2.5]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Where the light is (z up) |
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear; alpha is unused |
| `intensity` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Times the colour |
| `falloff` *(more)* | none \| inverse square | `"none"` |  | none: as bright at any distance; inverse square: as bright as the colour at 1 m, fading with distance |

### light.projector

A projector: throws its texture onto the geometry through a camera node's view

- `texture` (tex)

| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear; alpha is unused |
| `intensity` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Times the colour |
| `shadows` | bool | `true` |  | What stands in its way casts a shadow |
| `falloff` *(more)* | none \| inverse square | `"none"` |  | none: as bright at any distance; inverse square: as bright as the colour at 1 m, fading with distance |
| `bias` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Shadow offset, times the usual: more against stripes on lit surfaces, less against light leaking where objects touch |

### light.spot

Light from a point, in a cone towards the target

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (light).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | vec3 | `[0, -3, 3]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Where the light is (z up) |
| `target` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | What it shines at |
| `angle` | float | `45` | 5 to 120 ° (soft) | The whole cone, edge to edge |
| `softness` | float | `0.2` | 0 to 1 | How much of the cone fades towards its edge; 0 is a hard edge |
| `color` | colour | `[1, 1, 1, 1]` |  | Linear; alpha is unused |
| `intensity` | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Times the colour |
| `shadows` | bool | `false` |  | What stands in its way casts a shadow |
| `falloff` *(more)* | none \| inverse square | `"none"` |  | none: as bright at any distance; inverse square: as bright as the colour at 1 m, fading with distance |
| `bias` *(more)* | float | `1` | 0 to 4 (soft) | Shadow offset, times the usual: more against stripes on lit surfaces, less against light leaking where objects touch |

## view

[view.camera](#viewcamera)

### view.camera

A camera: where it is, what it looks at, its lens; for tex.render's camera input

Inputs: none.

Outputs: `out` (view).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | vec3 | `[2.4, -3.2, 1.6]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | Where the camera is (z up) |
| `target` | vec3 | `[0, 0, 0]` | -10 to 10 (soft) | What it looks at |
| `fov` | float | `40` | 5 to 120 ° (soft) | Vertical field of view |
| `roll` | float | `0` | -180 to 180 ° (soft) | Turn about the view axis; positive tilts the picture's top to the right |
| `shift` *(more)* | vec2 | `[0, 0]` | -1 to 1 (soft) | Lens shift in picture sizes: [0, 0.5] moves the picture up by half its height |
| `camera` *(more)* | text |  |  | A calibrated camera as JSON (calib.solve's `camera`); replaces position, target, fov, roll and shift |
| `near` *(more)* | float | `0.05` | 0.0001 to 10000 | Nearest distance drawn |
| `far` *(more)* | float | `100` | 0.001 to 1000000 | Farthest distance drawn |

## script

[script.python](#scriptpython)

### script.python

A Python script: cook(cx) turns channels and tables in into channels and a table out

Declares further params per node, from its file or code.

Inputs:

- `chan0` (chan)
- `chan1` (chan)
- `table0` (table)
- `table1` (table)

Outputs: `out` (chan), `table` (table).

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | file (py) |  |  | A .py file used instead of `code`, relative to the project; reloads when saved |
| `cook` | auto \| every frame \| on change | `"auto"` |  | When cook(cx) runs: auto = every frame if the code mentions `time` or `frame`, else when an input or a param changes |
| `timeout` | float | `0.1` | 0.01 to 1 s (soft) | A call running longer is stopped, and the node with it until the script changes |
| `code` | text | an example script |  | The script while `file` is empty |

## out

[out.projector](#outprojector)

### out.projector

A projector: shows its input fullscreen on a display, or in a part of it

Follows the show clock: cooks again whenever time moves.

Inputs:

- `in` (tex)

Outputs: none.

| param | type | default | range | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | text |  |  | Display id from output.list, e.g. `EPSON PJ @ port 4`; the monitor name alone works when unique |
| `active` | bool | `true` |  | Open the output window |
| `fit` | fit \| fill \| stretch | `"fit"` |  | fit: all visible, black bars; fill: covered, cropped; stretch: covered, distorted |
| `viewport` *(more)* | vec4 | `[0, 0, 1, 1]` | 0 to 1 | x, y, width, height inside the display, in display sizes (a quarter of a 4K splitter: 0, 0, 0.5, 0.5) |
| `test` | bool | `false` |  | A test pattern in the projector's own pixels instead of the input: square cells, centre, circle, and the image's edge in this projector's colour |
